7981.text: I'm Daniel James, and you're listening to 7am. The latest NAPLAN results show around a third of Australian students are still falling short in literacy and numeracy, results that have barely budged since 2023. At the same time, Australia has been settling a decades-long fight over how children should be taught to read. For years, many schools relied on outdated methods and encouraged children to work out words using context, pictures and other cues. Now, some classrooms are increasingly moving towards phonics and explicit instruction. But the evidence of that approach has been around for decades. So why is it taking so long for classrooms to catch up?
